title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
data_curation: Labels are never used by TTPO. Two settings: (1) OpenThoughts, where models train on OpenThoughts problems whose labels exist but are used only by the GRPO/OPSD comparison baselines; (2) pure test-time training (TTT), where the training set is the unlabeled test set itself (AIME 2026, HMMT 2026, BRUMO 2025). Supervision comes from majority voting over K=64 rollouts per problem (max 16,000 tokens to avoid truncation before answer extraction). Answers are clustered by mathematical equivalence; the largest cluster becomes the pseudo-label and splits rollouts into agreeing (positive) and disagreeing (negative) sets. On AIME 2026 with Qwen3-1.7B the pseudo-label is wrong for about 85% of prompts, yet about 79% of disagreeing rollouts are also wrong, which motivates the design.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. TTPO is a single 100-step LoRA training run (checkpoints every 25 steps) applied directly to Qwen3 models, with no SFT stage and a fixed objective throughout. The authors report a self-evolving loop instead of a curriculum: as training proceeds, single-sample Avg@12 rises toward the base Maj@12, and Maj@12 itself rises (HMMT26 33.3 to 42.4), so the pseudo-labels improve with the model. A dynamic schedule for lambda or the positive/negative ratio is left to future work.
method: TTPO is an asymmetric objective: agreeing rollouts get on-policy self-distillation (OPSD), a per-token forward KL from an answer-conditioned teacher (the same frozen base model, LoRA disabled, thinking mode on, pseudo-label in its prompt) to the thinking-off student. Disagreeing rollouts get only GRPO penalties (binary reward = matches majority), which are label-agnostic. Token selection: distillation weights w(t) are a Soft-OR of min-max-normalized student entropy and teacher-student KL, down-weighting converged positions; the GRPO branch masks to the top 50% of tokens by s(t) = -log p * (1 - normalized entropy), so only confident errors are penalized. Loss = L_OPSD + lambda*L_GRPO with lambda=0.1. Each step uses K_train=8 rollouts (fixed 50/50 positive/negative, shortest selected); gradients use only the first 1,024 completion tokens. LoRA r=64, alpha=128 on all linear layers, LR 5e-6, batch 32, temperature 1.1, full-vocabulary logit distillation, 4xH20.
eval_metrics: Avg@12 at temperature 1.0 with thinking enabled (max 38,912 new tokens) on AIME 2025, AIME 2026, HMMT 2025, HMMT 2026 and BRUMO 2025; Maj@12 tracked during TTT; non-thinking evaluation in the appendix. Reported scores are the peak over saved checkpoints (100 steps for OPSD/TTPO, 500 for GRPO/TTRL). OpenThoughts-setting average: 40.1 / 58.6 / 62.6 for 1.7B / 4B / 8B, versus label-supervised OPSD 39.7 / 58.4 / 61.7 and GRPO 35.7 / 57.5 / 61.2. TTT average: 45.2 / 61.1 / 65.3, versus TTRL 40.2 / 58.8 / 63.0 and OPSD-TTT 41.9 / 59.4 / 63.7. Non-thinking gains over base: +25.2 / +30.6 / +36.4, versus +7.1 / +5.8 / +3.5 for OPSD.
key_results: Without any labels, TTPO matches or beats ground-truth-supervised OPSD at all three Qwen3 scales, and in pure TTT lifts Qwen3-1.7B from 38.0 to 45.2 average (+5.4 over TTRL, +3.3 over OPSD-TTT). Qwen3-4B with TTPO (61.1) surpasses the Qwen3-8B base (60.7). Swapping pseudo-labels for ground truth performs worse, because on hard problems the correct-answer positive set is nearly empty and both branches starve.
evolution_note: TTPO combines two 2026 lines: TTRL-style label-free test-time RL with majority-vote rewards (and follow-ups Hi-TTRL and SCRL), and OPSD-style on-policy self-distillation with a privileged-information teacher (and hybrids that mix OPSD with RLVR). It responds to the fragility of pseudo-label distillation, where a wrong vote corrupts every token, with a negative-learning argument: penalizing disagreement stays correct even when the vote is wrong. Its token weighting and masking borrow from TIP and STAPO. It extends dense self-distillation to settings where labels never arrive, though only on verifiable math so far.
